recognize_zh: 周邊血液中一顆嗜中性球的細胞質內有一團深藍紫色、呈桑椹狀（morula）的點狀包涵體，靠近細胞核旁，是人類顆粒球無形體症（human granulocytic anaplasmosis）的特徵。
features: Segmented neutrophil with a cytoplasmic basophilic stippled inclusion forming a mulberry-like cluster (morula)
Morula located adjacent to the nucleus, composed of tightly packed dark blue-purple granular elements
Neutrophil cytoplasm with prominent coarse granulation (toxic-type change)
Background red cells with echinocytes/crenated forms and occasional irregular shapes
A small platelet clump at the upper left; no intraerythrocytic parasites
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a segmented neutrophil containing a dark blue-purple, mulberry-shaped cytoplasmic inclusion (morula) composed of clustered granular elements adjacent to the nucleus. The neutrophil cytoplasm shows coarse granulation. Red cells include crenated forms, and no intraerythrocytic organisms are seen. In a patient with fever, respiratory failure and a subacute febrile illness, findings are consistent with human granulocytic anaplasmosis (Anaplasma phagocytophilum); PCR of whole blood is the confirmatory test, since morulae are seen in only a minority of cases.

ddx.vs: E. chaffeensis morulae occur mainly in monocytes rather than neutrophils; PCR distinguishes the species.
Döhle bodies are pale blue, homogeneous, peripheral cytoplasmic patches and toxic granules are dispersed, whereas a morula is a discrete, stippled, dark cluster.
Phagocytosed bacteria are discrete cocci/rods and Histoplasma yeasts have clear halos, rather than a single membrane-bound cluster of tiny granules.
A platelet lying on a neutrophil has a granular purple center with a pale hyalomere and is in a slightly different focal plane.
